_schema.note: Provenance for Tier 1 editorial sentences. One entry per player slug. Nothing renders without an entry here; a slug absent from this file gets no editorial sentence, which is the 'omit rather than pad' rule working correctly.
_schema.sources: A LIST, not a single URL — a sentence may make more than one independent claim, and one page rarely substantiates all of them. Each source carries the verbatim quote that supports its claim, so re-verification survives link rot.
_schema.falsifiable_by_game: Explicit author assertion. 'Game' means ANY game, not just a WNBA one — a college record is falsified by a college game, a school record by a future player at that school. Must be false for the sentence to ship.
_schema.validator: sites/wnba/validate_hooks.py (to be written) — asserts every rendered slug has an entry, every entry has >=1 source with a non-empty quote, and falsifiable_by_game is false.

_rejected.note: Kept deliberately. These were checkpoint placeholders that did NOT survive the falsifiability rule. Recorded so nobody re-proposes them in six months.

caitlin-clark.rejected_sentence: The NCAA's all-time leading scorer — men's or women's — and the first pick of the 2024 draft.
caitlin-clark.reason: Two independent failures in one clause. (1) 'All-time leading scorer' is falsifiable by a COLLEGE game — the rule was misapplied to WNBA games only, and nothing in our build would catch the day it stops being true. (2) The 'men's or women's' framing is contested: the record is NCAA Division I, and Pearl Moore's pre-NCAA total is the standard objection. The draft clause alone is durable and could be re-proposed on its own — but it duplicates the generated facts sentence, so it earns nothing.

sonia-citron.rejected_sentence: The third pick of the 2025 draft and an All-Rookie selection that year — the only player in Notre Dame history with 1,700 points, 700 rebounds and 300 assists.
sonia-citron.reason: The compound superlative is falsifiable by a future Notre Dame player and is hard to source to a primary reference. The draft position and All-Rookie selection are durable, but both are the kind of fact the generated sentence already carries, so what remains does not justify an editorial slot.
